To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mmedIC can self reconfigure its energy harvesting and backscatter capabilities to adapt to in body environments.
mmedIC can self-reconfigure its energy harvesting and data rate to adapt to different in-body environments.
We built a batteryless, wireless, self reconfigurable micro implant that can operate across different in-body tissues and channel conditions, and that we evaluated it in vitro and ex vivo conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) design of a fully integrated wireless sensor that can operate in complex in body environments, and (b) design of a backscatter based communication scheme that allows the sensor to self reconfigure and adapt to these environments.
the design, implementation and evaluation of mIC, a fully wireless and batteryless millimeter sized sensor that can self-reconfigure its energy harvesting resonance and backscatter bitrate.
the development of a fully integrated micro implanted sensor that is capable of self reconfiguration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper is a significant advance for the field of wireless body area network and the authors have done an excellent job in the implementation and evaluation.

we have designed, implemented, and evaluated a fully integrated wireless micro implanted sensor which is able to self adapt to different tissues, thus enabling it to communicate across different in body environments and support high throughput applications.
we present a new design for a wireless and batteryless cross tissue sensor that can self adapt its energy harvesting resonance and backscatter rate to support higher data rates and availability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the design, implementation and evaluation of a fully integrated wireless micro implanted sensor which can adapt to different tissue and channel conditions.

we have developed a new class of batteryless micro implants which can adapt to different tissues, scale their data rates and energy consumption to meet the application needs, and operate at low power to extend their lifetime.
we have demonstrated the first batteryless micro implant that can adapt to different tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in body environment is not a fixed environment, but rather one that is dynamic, and that the next generation of wireless and batteryless in body devices must adapt to these changes in order to operate in the most challenging of in body environments.

by combining self tuning energy harvesting, backscatter rate adaptation, and low power circuits, we can design a fully integrated wireless sensor that is capable of powering up, communicating, and adapting to a variety of in vivo conditions.
the design and operation of micro implants can be greatly enhanced by exploiting their self reconfigurability.
